ai.title: CI test retry maxattempts set to 5
ai.summary: Reverted CI workflow retry configuration in .github/workflows/ci.yml, increasing max_attempts for the bun test step from 1 to 5. This change addresses flaky test execution by allowing up to five retry attempts within the 10-minute timeout window. Scope limited to GitHub Actions CI pipeline configuration.

eli5.text: The automated system that checks the code for problems before it gets added now gives failing tests more chances to pass on their own. Instead of giving up after a single failure, it will retry a flaky test up to five times before declaring a real problem. This affects the internal team that writes and checks the assistant software; to them, some temporary test failures that used to require a manual rerun will now resolve themselves without intervention. The change is live as of the latest code check-in and applies only to the pre-merge test runs that gate code changes.

ai.title: CI: Drop CODEBUFFGITHUBACTIONS, Re-enable tmate debug shell
ai.summary: CI pipeline stops injecting `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` into `.env.local` for build and test jobs. `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` debug shell restored on failure in `ci.yml`.

eli5.text: When the code-checking process runs and something goes wrong, the team can now open a live debugging session to investigate the problem directly. The automated scripts that run during code checks stopped adding an extra setting that told the system it was running inside GitHub's environment, so builds and tests now run without that extra flag attached.

ai.title: Update main prompt stop conditions
ai.summary: Replaced GPT-4.1-specific 'do not end turn' instruction with a universal directive to stop immediately upon completion. Removed the conditional logic for `isGPT4_1` in the primary instruction block, simplifying the prompt structure. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. New rule explicitly forbids further refinements after initial completion.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to do something, it will now stop more quickly once it thinks it's done, rather than endlessly double-checking its own work. It no longer treats one specific advanced model differently from others when deciding when to wrap up. If you gave it a complex task with multiple possible interpretations, it will still ask a clarifying question first, but only if you didn't explicitly tell it to just go ahead.

ai.title: CI test command switched to cd + bun test
ai.summary: The CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` now executes tests via `cd ${{ matrix.package }} && bun test` instead of `bun test $(find ${{ matrix.package }}/src -name *.test.ts)`. This change ensures `bun test` runs within the package directory context, likely to resolve module paths or configuration correctly that the previous `find` approach missed.

eli5.text: Starting May 15, 2025, the CI workflow changed how tests are executed from 'run tests using a list of specific test files' to 'navigate to the package directory and run all tests.' This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping for internal contributors and affects how automated checks are performed during development. You wouldn't notice this directly unless you're reviewing CI logs, but it simplifies test execution by relying on the package context rather than manually finding individual test files.

ai.title: CI test discovery and debug shell changes
ai.summary: CI test commands now use `find src -name *.test.ts` for explicit discovery. Interactive debug shell step via `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` commented out. Affects `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

eli5.text: The automated test step now runs only the specific test files it is told to, instead of guessing which ones to run. The team also turned off a diagnostic tool that developers could open to poke around when a test failed, which makes that failure path a little less convenient to investigate. This is internal housekeeping for the project's build system, so most people won't notice it directly.

ai.title: Add endturn tool for explicit turn termination
ai.summary: Introduced `end_turn` tool to allow agents to explicitly finish their turn, overriding pending tool results. Updated backend prompt, tool schemas, and client handlers to recognize this signal. Eval scaffolding and npm-app client now break loops or set completion flags when `end_turn` is called. Renderer suppresses visual output for this tool.

eli5.text: The assistant can now explicitly signal when it is finished with a turn by invoking a new action called end_turn. When this action is used, the system stops processing any further results the assistant may have queued and hands control back to you, so you can type your next message instead of waiting for more output. In practice, you will see the conversation simply end and your turn to reply begin whenever the assistant chooses to call this new action, rather than the previous default of continuing until no more tool calls remained. This behavior is live today across the agent backend and the npm-app client.

ai.title: Bump npm-app version to 1.0.283
ai.summary: npm-app/package.json version field updated from 1.0.282 to 1.0.283. Package metadata change only. No functional code modifications.

eli5.text: The software you use quietly bumped its internal version label to a new number today, which is the kind of routine bookkeeping that keeps installations running smoothly behind the scenes. That label also shipped a small batch of improvements you might actually notice if you use it: the assistant can now end a turn on purpose instead of guessing when to stop, and it now tells the difference between messages you typed and system notes it receives. A few behind-the-scenes changes also tightened up how things are logged and tested, plus a fix so error messages now include the exact file path when something fails to write. None of this is something you'd see in the interface directly, but it makes the experience steadier and a bit more predictable.

ai.title: Fix message history filter return in main-prompt
ai.summary: Corrects a missing return statement in the messageHistory filter callback within backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Previously, the arrow function body lacked explicit return, causing the filter to always evaluate to undefined and effectively deleting all history entries. This restores intended behavior for filtering system instructions.

eli5.text: When the system built your assistant's prompt, it was supposed to clear out any leftover system instruction messages from the conversation history before adding the fresh ones. Due to a small bug, the filter that removes those messages silently failed and instead wiped your entire conversation history. The fix makes that filter work correctly again, so your past messages are preserved while only the system instructions get replaced.

You wouldn't see it directly; it only matters if you look at the raw output the assistant uses when it reads a file, where you'd now notice the tag appearing alongside the file path and contents. This tag is just a label for now, like a name tag that nothing actively checks yet, so no behavior you interact with changes today.

ai.title: Relax whitespace regex in parseReadFilesResult
ai.summary: Updated the `filePattern` regex in `backend/src/util/parse-tool-call-xml.ts` to accept variable whitespace instead of strict newlines. This prevents parsing failures when `read_file` XML blocks contain extra spaces or tabs between tags. Affects internal tool result parsing for file reads.

eli5.text: Internal code that turns read-file results from the new tool-call format into a normal shape now ignores extra spaces, tabs, or blank lines between the XML tags. Previously, even a single stray space or tab could make the parser silently fail to extract the file contents, so any tool that asked to read a file might come back empty when invoked through this path. This only affects internal tool result parsing, not anything you'd see directly.

ai.title: runMainPrompt accepts sessionId, costMode normal
ai.summary: runMainPrompt now takes sessionId argument. loopMainPrompt generates unique test-session-id per run. costMode changed from experimental to normal. Internal evals scaffolding tweak only.

eli5.text: Each time the internal evaluation loops run, they now assign a unique session identifier to every test run instead of reusing the same one. The cost calculation method switched from its experimental setting to the normal setting. Both changes apply only to the behind-the-scenes testing tooling used internally today.

ai.title: Clarify user cwd vs assistant cwd in system prompt
ai.summary: The system prompt injected when `cwd` is present now explicitly labels it as `**user** cwd` and notes that the assistant's working directory is the project root. This change aims to reduce ambiguity for the model regarding which directory context applies to user commands versus agent operations. The update is localized to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` within the `mainPrompt` function's context injection logic. The previous format only specified `cwd: <path>`, which could lead to confusion about the agent's actual execution environment relative to the user's shell context.

eli5.text: The system now explicitly tells the AI the difference between the folder you are working in and the folder the AI uses by default, clearing up confusion that could happen when you ask it to run commands in a specific place. If you looked at the settings, you'd see the working folder you're referring to is now labeled clearly as yours, with a note that the AI's home base stays where the project lives. This is a small wording fix that went live today and only affects how the AI understands your location versus its own.

Cache control logic in `getMessagesSubset` now preserves the marker only on the last cached message. Internal change to message history handling and prompt construction.

eli5.text: When you have a long conversation with the assistant, the system now takes any messages the assistant previously sent, wraps them in special tags to mark them as old assistant messages, and repackages them as if they came from you (the user). This is a behind-the-scenes change to how the backend builds prompts from conversation history; it does not change anything you currently see or experience, because the new behavior is present in code but not yet turned on. Today, you will notice nothing different.

ai.title: Deterministic file tree sampling via seedrandom
ai.summary: Replaced non-deterministic `sampleSize` with `sampleSizeWithSeed` in `truncate-file-tree.ts` to ensure consistent token budget estimation. The new utility in `common/src/util/random.ts` uses `seedrandom` for a Fisher-Yates shuffle, seeded by the JSON string of the file list and sample count. This change affects backend system prompt generation and adds `@types/seedrandom` to `common/package.json`. Identical inputs now yield identical sampling results, preventing flaky truncation behavior.

eli5.text: When the assistant looks at your files to decide how much to keep and how much to cut, it used to pick the sample files using randomness that could change every time, so the same set of files could lead to slightly different estimates. Now it uses a fixed, deterministic method seeded by the file list itself, so the same files always produce the same sample and the same token estimate. You as a user would notice that the system prompt generation behaves consistently instead of showing occasional drift or flakiness in how your file context gets truncated. This fix applies to the backend service that builds system prompts for the assistant and has been live as of today's date.

ai.title: Add explicit endturn tool prompting to agent instructions
ai.summary: System prompts in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md` now explicitly require the `end_turn` tool. This ensures agents correctly signal completion or wait for user input, preventing premature stops. The change applies to both lite and standard modes.

eli5.text: The AI helper now ends each of its answers with a small signal that tells the system it's done talking, so it won't interrupt you mid-task or stop prematurely while still working. This applies to everyone using the assistant, in both the fast and full modes. If you looked, you'd see the helper append this signal to the end of every completed response.
